introduction: “What is Satan?” someone asked ‘Abdu’l-Bahá, and he answered, “The insistent self.” The readings work this out. There is no personal devil and no satanic half of humanity; all are leaves of one tree. What the scriptures call Satan is the ego: its first act was to think itself better, and it whispers, takes attractive forms, and speaks most dangerously “in the name of truth.” Bahá’u’lláh’s many warnings to stand firm are then read as warnings about one’s own steadfastness, and the last reading forbids contention even with Satan. The Bible and the Qur’án are quoted on both sides of the question. They speak of the heart, the soul that commands evil, and a tempter who admits he can only call; they also speak of a roaring lion and an enemy to be treated as one. Augustine, Milton, Shakespeare, Dostoevsky and the Dhammapada are here for the inward reading, and Jude for the archangel who would not revile even the devil.
questions: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá says Satan has no personal identity; the First Letter of Peter speaks of an adversary who “walketh about.” What practical difference does it make which way a person thinks of temptation?

“He does not say, Ye are the leaves of two trees: one divine, the other satanic.” What has followed in history when people believed in the second tree, and what does the parable of the wheat and tares say to that?
In the Qur’án Satan says, “I had no power over you save that I called unto you and ye obeyed me.” How does this fit ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s answer, and where does it leave responsibility?
Satan fell “as soon as he began to see himself.” Why is self-regard treated as the root, here and in Isaiah, Ezekiel and Milton?
“The satans … [lie] in wait in the name of truth,” and Paul speaks of an angel of light. How does one test an impulse that presents itself as righteous?
The last reading forbids contention even with Satan, and Jude’s archangel would not revile him. How is vigilance different from enmity, toward oneself and toward opponents?

outside.why: “What is Satan?” “The insistent self.” The phrase comes from the Qur’án, where Joseph says: I do not exculpate myself; the human soul enjoineth unto evil.
James traces temptation to the same place: every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.
“The first self-conceited one was Satan.” The Qur’án gives his words when told to honour Adam: I am better than him. Thou createdst me of fire while him Thou didst create of mud.
“Ye are all the leaves of one tree,” and there is no second, satanic tree. Paul at Athens: God hath made of one blood all nations of men.

No part of humanity belongs to Satan. In John’s Gospel Jesus says to hostile hearers: ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do. What has been done in history with words like these, and how does ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s reading of Satan as the self prevent it?

One tree, not two. Jesus’ parable has two sowings in one field and forbids the servants to sort them: let both grow together until the harvest. How near does that come to ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s refusal to divide humanity?
“There is a devil within man, just as there is the divine voice within man.” Dmitri Karamazov: God and the devil are fighting there and the battlefield is the heart of man.
The Pharisee’s self-righteousness “was his devil.” The prayer in question: God, I thank thee, that I am not as other men are.

“Anything … that makes you become heedless of God is your Satan.” Jesus gave the name to his closest disciple for a well-meant word: get thee behind me, Satan: thou savourest not the things that be of God, but those that be of men.
“Personal identity of the devil is not true.” Jesus on where evil comes from: from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts.

No personal devil. The First Letter of Peter speaks of one as plainly as of any person: your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour. What does a believer gain, and what might he lose, by reading the lion as his own ego?
The ego “at every minute and hour wants to overcome them.” Paul: the good that I would I do not: but the evil which I would not, that I do.
In the Qur’án Satan himself disclaims any power but suggestion: I had no power over you save that I called unto you and ye obeyed me. So blame me not, but blame yourselves.
The contest is with oneself. Proverbs: he that ruleth his spirit is better than he that taketh a city.
“Outwardly some individuals are refined and presentable, but in their essence they remain base.” Richard III: and seem a saint, when most I play the devil.
The call of Satan is to “the pursuit of self and passion … love of the world.” Augustine: two cities have been formed by two loves: the earthly by the love of self, even to the contempt of God.
“Vanity is one of the characteristics of Satan.” The First Letter to Timothy warns against promoting a novice, lest being lifted up with pride he fall into the condemnation of the devil.

He was “favored at the Threshold of God” until “he began to see himself.” Ezekiel’s lament, long read as the story of that fall: thou art the anointed cherub; thine heart was lifted up because of thy beauty.
Isaiah: how art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning! For thou hast said in thine heart, I will ascend into heaven.
He said, “I am the most noble, the most high.” Milton gave the fallen angel his best-known line: better to reign in Hell than serve in Heaven.

‘Abdu’l-Bahá recalls the mountain-top. Matthew: the devil sheweth him all the kingdoms of the world, and the glory of them; and saith, All these things will I give thee, if thou wilt fall down and worship me.
The Báb quotes the last chapter of the Qur’án, a prayer for refuge from the one who whispereth in the hearts of mankind.
Whose whisper is it? Elsewhere the Qur’án says: We know what his soul whispereth to him, and We are nearer to him than his jugular vein.
“People are weak” and even the trusting are troubled by doubts. Jesus to Peter: Satan hath desired to have you, that he may sift you as wheat: but I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not.
“The satans have been and are lying in wait in the name of truth.” Paul: Satan himself is transformed into an angel of light.
“Satan appears in various forms and likenesses.” The Merchant of Venice: the devil can cite Scripture for his purpose.
“Satan hath lurked in every pathway.” His vow in the Qur’án: I shall lurk in ambush for them on Thy Right Path.
“Gird yourselves against his wicked devices.” The Letter to the Ephesians: put on the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil.
“Exert your utmost effort and striving.” The Dhammapada: self is the lord of self, who else could be the lord? With self well subdued, a man finds a lord such as few can find.
“Stand firm in that whereunto thou hast attained.” James: resist the devil, and he will flee from you. Draw nigh to God, and he will draw nigh to you.
“Seek ye refuge in God.” The Qur’án on the limit of the tempter: he hath no power over those who believe and put trust in their Lord.
“Today the All-Merciful is manifest and Satan is evident.” Jesus to the seventy returning from their mission: I beheld Satan as lightning fall from heaven.
“Soon will Satan call out in the name of the All-Merciful.” In the wilderness the tempter came with a verse of the Psalms: for it is written, He shall give his angels charge concerning thee.
The prayer niche “is the place of battle with Satan.” God to Cain, before the first murder: sin lieth at the door. And unto thee shall be his desire, and thou shalt rule over him.
A battle. The Qur’án uses the word of an outward fight and adds an estimate of the enemy: the devil’s strategy is ever weak. What changes when the battlefield is moved to the place of prayer?

“Contention even with Satan is not permissible.” The Letter of Jude: Michael the archangel, when contending with the devil, durst not bring against him a railing accusation, but said, The Lord rebuke thee.

No contention, even with Satan. The Qur’án: the devil is an enemy for you, so treat him as an enemy. How can a person be vigilant against the self, as the earlier readings ask, without the strife that this last reading forbids?

corinthians-angel-of-light.text: For such are false apostles, deceitful workers, transforming themselves into the apostles of Christ. And no marvel; for Satan himself is transformed into an angel of light. Therefore it is no great thing if his ministers also be transformed as the ministers of righteousness; whose end shall be according to their works

jude-durst-not-bring-a-railing-accusatio.text: Yet Michael the archangel, when contending with the devil he disputed about the body of Moses, durst not bring against him a railing accusation, but said, The Lord rebuke thee

luke-satan-as-lightning-fall.text: And the seventy returned again with joy, saying, Lord, even the devils are subject unto us through thy name. And he said unto them, I beheld Satan as lightning fall from heaven. Behold, I give unto you power to tread on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy: and nothing shall by any means hurt you. Notwithstanding in this rejoice not, that the spirits are subject unto you; but rather rejoice, because your names are written in heaven

job-going-to-and-fro-in-the-earth.text: Now there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the Lord, and Satan came also among them. And the Lord said unto Satan, Whence comest thou? Then Satan answered the Lord, and said, From going to and fro in the earth, and from walking up and down in it

ezekiel-heart-lifted-up-because-of-thy-b.text: Thou art the anointed cherub that covereth; and I have set thee so: thou wast upon the holy mountain of God; thou hast walked up and down in the midst of the stones of fire. Thou wast perfect in thy ways from the day that thou wast created, till iniquity was found in thee. By the multitude of thy merchandise they have filled the midst of thee with violence, and thou hast sinned: therefore I will cast thee as profane out of the mountain of God: and I will destroy thee, O covering cherub, from the midst of the stones of fire. Thine heart was lifted up because of thy beauty, thou hast corrupted thy wisdom by reason of thy brightness

john-ye-are-of-your-father-the-devil.text: Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do. He was a murderer from the beginning, and abode not in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he speaketh a lie, he speaketh of his own: for he is a liar, and the father of it

james-resist-the-devil.text: Submit yourselves therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you. Draw nigh to God, and he will draw nigh to you

quran-devil-is-an-enemy-treat-him-as-an-.text: Lo! the devil is an enemy for you, so treat him as an enemy. He only summoneth his faction to be owners of the flaming Fire.

quran-lurk-in-ambush-on-thy-right-path.text: He said: Now, because Thou hast sent me astray, verily I shall lurk in ambush for them on Thy Right Path.

quran-blame-me-not-but-blame-yourselves.text: And Satan saith, when the matter hath been decided: Lo! Allah promised you a promise of truth; and I promised you, then failed you. And I had no power over you save that I called unto you and ye obeyed me. So blame not, but blame yourselves. I cannot help you, nor can ye help me, Lo! I disbelieved in that which ye before ascribed to me. Lo! for wrong-doers is a painful doom.

quran-devils-strategy-is-ever-weak.text: Those who believe do battle for the cause of Allah; and those who disbelieve do battle for the cause of idols. So fight the minions of the devil. Lo! the devil's strategy is ever weak.

quran-whispereth-in-the-hearts-of-mankin.text: Who whispereth in the hearts of mankind,

quran-no-power-over-those-who-believe.text: Lo! he hath no power over those who believe and put trust in their Lord.
